_comment: The browser-dom platform (DESIGN 1): one HTML file, drawn by a generic shell.
A definition that declares this platform must declare these types exactly, and
its interface must contain these five functions. $State is the record type
start returns; the other functions must use that same type. Which errors each
function raises is the app's to declare. The shell calls these and nothing else.
brief: how the shell calls the app, for whoever decides what to make; examples: how to pin it, for the tester.
name: browser-dom
brief: start is called when the app opens, with what was saved last time (or null).
step is called every second; act when the player presses a button (`action` is the button's action string); screen after every change; save after every change.
If act throws, the shell keeps the old state: an action that is not allowed throws.
Everything the player can do is an action string; an action that needs confirmation is two actions (one that asks, one that confirms), and the state remembers the question.

screen returns a Screen: a title and a vertical list of nodes -- a heading, a text, or a button (with its action and whether it is enabled). Non-button nodes have action "" and enabled true. That is the whole vocabulary.
examples: Pin the screen where an item is about it: examples of screen for a few states, judged by `matches` on the nodes the item is about. Write the whole screen out only when the item is about all of it.
